## Analysis

**Reading the logs (task_score ≈ achieved forward speed, in m/s):**

| Candidate | @iter 500 | max | recent growth (last 150 it) | key property |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C2 | 7.45 | 8.10 | +0.5…+0.8 / 50 it | tanh(T=10) + linear ramp to 14 m/s (no early saturation) |
| C4 | 7.21 | 7.84 | +0.2…+0.5 / 50 it | tanh(T=6) + surge ramp, but **saturates at 9.5 m/s** |
| C3 | 5.98 | 6.16 | +0.25 / 50 it | tanh(T=6) + 0.2·v linear, small tilt cost |
| C1 | 5.25 | 5.49 | +0.38 / 50 it | linear speed **multiplicatively gated by uprightness** |

**Why C2 wins:** it is the only design that keeps a usable speed gradient in the regime that matters. Its tanh(T=10) term plus the "faster than 5 m/s" ramp gives ~0.075 reward/m/s at 8 m/s and still ~0.05 at 12 m/s. Crucially, C2 only penalizes *tipped-over* postures (up_z < 0.4) and has weak posture shaping (0.15 weight, linear in up_z), so the ant is free to pitch its torso to sprint — exactly what is needed to break past ~8–10 m/s. Its soft joint-limit term (0.05) is the only meaningful brake and is mild.

**Why C4 is second, not first:** its surge ramp is the strongest single gradient up to ~9.5 m/s (0.14/m/s), which is why it led early (3.08 vs 2.16 at iter 100). But the ramp *clips* at 9.5 m/s, and its tanh(T=6) is nearly flat beyond ~12 m/s; meanwhile `upright` (exp, weight 0.6) and `heading_align` (0.4·fwd_x) both penalize torso pitch, an increasingly binding brake as the ant tries to sprint. So C4's reward gradient effectively dies around 9–11 m/s, while C2's keeps pushing.

**Why C3 > C1:** C3's linear term (0.2·v, unclipped to 15 m/s) is un-gated and its tilt cost is only quadratic and tiny; it also has an alive bonus protecting episode length. C1's reward is `speed × uprightness`, so any forward lean immediately discounts the speed term, plus the `uprightness` bonus keeps the torso pinned vertical — a self-limiting loop exactly in the sprinting regime. C1's larger raw reward scale also means larger advantages against a fixed PPO clip, which tends to saturate the surrogate and slow progress (consistent with its slower climb). C3 is already ahead by ~0.7 m/s and its shaping degrades more gracefully at high speed.

**Prediction:** C2 (≈11–13 m/s) > C4 (≈9.5–11 m/s) > C3 (≈7–8.5 m/s) > C1 (≈6–7.5 m/s) by iteration 3,000.
